comments.title: Preserve signal status during dependency setup
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve signal status during dependency setup**

When SIGINT or SIGTERM arrives during the automatic Bun dependency setup, the new handler forwards it to the child and waits, but this branch converts the resulting signal status into `fail(...)`, which always exits 2. Thus cancelling a first invocation during installation no longer returns the conventional 130/143 status that `exit_status()` preserves for the actual helper, making callers unable to distinguish cancellation from a setup error; exit with `exit_status(setup)` here as well.

comments.title: Report all unstaged files after an interrupt
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Report all unstaged files after an interrupt**

If Ctrl-C occurs while `_temp()` is staging the second or a later change, that current entry and every subsequent entry have not yet been appended to `staged`, so this comprehension omits them from `skipped`. The CLI consequently emits a partial result that accounts for neither all applied nor all pending setup files, despite presenting the accepted plan as resumable; derive `skipped` from the full `changes` list instead.

comments.title: Make retry branch creation recoverable
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make retry branch creation recoverable**

GitHub keeps `GITHUB_RUN_ID` unchanged when a failed workflow run is retried. If the first attempt pushes this branch and then fails before `gh pr create` completes, the retry creates a new sibling commit from the default branch and its push is rejected as non-fast-forward, so rerunning cannot finish the draft PR. Include `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` in the branch name or detect and reuse the already-pushed branch and commit.

comments.title: Persist reproduction evidence before the runner exits
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Persist reproduction evidence before the runner exits**

The reproduce contract requires captures under `control.artifact_directory` and a link to that evidence in the source comment and draft-PR proof, but the complete workflow contains no artifact upload or other publication step before reading and posting `source_comment_body` here. On `ubuntu-latest`, `/tmp/intake-artifacts` disappears at job teardown, leaving reviewers unable to inspect the evidence used to justify the generated patch. Upload the captures with a pinned action and publish a durable artifact reference.

comments.title: Preserve cancellation during runtime discovery
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve cancellation during runtime discovery**

When SIGINT or SIGTERM arrives while `--version` is running, `runProcess` correctly returns `cancelled: true`, but this branch converts that outcome into `UnsupportedError`, so the receipt reports `UNSUPPORTED` rather than `CANCELLED`. The launcher’s `forward` handler in `plugins/cstack/scripts/run_tool.py` makes this reachable whenever a user cancels during discovery, and it incorrectly records a capability gap instead of the actual task outcome. Propagate cancellation as `CANCELLED` here, as is already done for the worker process.

comments.title: Await process-group shutdown after stdin errors
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Await process-group shutdown after stdin errors**

If Codex or Claude closes stdin while a large prompt is still being written—for example after an early authentication or argument failure—the stream emits `EPIPE` and this handler rejects immediately after sending only SIGTERM. Unlike the timeout and cancellation paths, it neither schedules SIGKILL nor waits for the process group to terminate, so a CLI descendant that ignores SIGTERM can remain running and continue writing after the runner has returned `FAILED`. Route this path through `stopGroup` and await shutdown before settling.

comments.title: Tolerate an interrupted final JSONL record
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Tolerate an interrupted final JSONL record**

If the process is killed or the write fails after only part of the last result has reached `results.jsonl`, this list comprehension sends the incomplete line directly to `json.loads`, raising `JSONDecodeError`. Both `run` and `report` then abort before the campaign can resume, contrary to the documented resumability guarantee; write records atomically or explicitly discard only an incomplete trailing record.

comments.title: Use a persistent thread for the cstack arm
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a persistent thread for the cstack arm**

This call delegates to `verify-behavior.run_case`, which always starts the app-server thread with `ephemeral: True`, while the cstack prompt explicitly authorizes a native Goal for multi-phase work. The repository's own Goal probe documents that ephemeral threads reject Goals (`docs/VERIFICATION.md`, line 279), so multi-phase cstack runs cannot exercise the workflow being evaluated and may fail or degrade while the vanilla arm is unaffected. Add a persistent-thread mode for these runs, applied consistently across arms, and clean up the resulting thread state afterward.

comments.title: Fail instead of silently skipping marketplace removal
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail instead of silently skipping marketplace removal**

`codex plugin marketplace remove --help` describes the command as “Remove a configured marketplace source by name,” but when `plugin marketplace list --json` fails because of an unreadable configuration, CLI error, or malformed output, `codex_state` suppresses that failure and returns an empty value here. The uninstall then skips marketplace removal and prints that cstack was removed even though its source remains configured; distinguish an absent marketplace from a failed state query, or attempt an idempotent removal before reporting success.

comments.title: Validate the plugin before replacing the marketplace
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the plugin before replacing the marketplace**

When `--ref` or `--local` points to a valid marketplace that does not contain a usable `cstack` plugin, this trial succeeds, the working marketplace is removed, and the later `plugin add` at line 145 fails outside the rollback block. This leaves the replacement marketplace configured and the previously installed plugin unavailable. I reproduced this with codex-cli 0.144.0-alpha.4 using a valid local marketplace with an empty plugin list; its help likewise treats `marketplace add` (“Add a local or Git marketplace”) and `plugin add` (“Install a plugin from a configured marketplace snapshot”) as separate operations. Run `plugin add` in the disposable home as part of validation, or restore the prior marketplace if the real plugin installation fails.

comments.title: Roll back the source when the final plugin install fails
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Roll back the source when the final plugin install fails**

When switching an existing source, if this production `plugin add` fails after disposable validation—for example because the real `CODEX_HOME` plugin cache is full or unwritable—`add_marketplace` has already removed the old marketplace and configured the replacement, but no rollback runs. The command therefore exits with a partially applied source change and potentially only the old cached plugin; fresh evidence beyond the earlier invalid-catalog issue is that this real-home installation remains outside the rollback block. I checked Codex CLI 0.144.0-alpha.4 help, which describes `plugin add` as “Install a plugin from a configured marketplace snapshot”; include this call in the source-change transaction and restore the previous source if it fails.

comments.title: Pin the exact previous commit for rollback
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin the exact previous commit for rollback**

When the existing marketplace tracks a branch whose remote has advanced since the last upgrade, and a source switch later fails after disposable validation, this prefers the symbolic branch name (for example `main`) over the checked-out commit. The rollback therefore fetches the branch's new tip instead of restoring the snapshot that was present before the command, potentially changing the installed plugin while reporting that the old source was restored. Codex CLI 0.144.0-alpha.4 documents `--ref` as the Git ref to fetch; record `rev-parse HEAD` here so rollback is pinned to the exact prior revision.

comments.title: Preserve the disabled state when refreshing the plugin
comments.body:

comments.body:
